content: The library of babel started as a thought experiment but this person built it digitally. It is an algorithm that produces books of a fixed length and all of the books together contain every possible combination of letters and spaces (up to the fixed length). This means you can search for any string and find it's pre-existing coordinate in the library. But browsing the library manually you could spend your whole life and never find anything meaningful. It's partially a proof of the scarcity of functionally specified information in an even distribution of chaos.

content:
- create a new nsec for each event
- sign the event with your real nsec
- encrypt the signed event with a conversation key derived from your real npub + the new nsec
- publish the encrypted event
- upon zapping we use existing infrastructure for zaps, but add a tag, nip44 encrypted to the zapper: the nsec
- zapper uses nsec to decrypt event

Ok, I figured out the problem and deployed a fix for it! Sorry for the wait! Maybe launching on a Friday is a bad idea 😅

The problem was your minibits lightning provider doesn't publish the P tag with the payer's pubkey which our payment verification checks for. However, the pubkey is also available in the description tag, so we now fallback to that. No problem!

Appreciate you trying it. I apologize for the problems but we just made our payment system more robust. Thanks again!

Everyone who has already purchased your note will be able to unlock it now. No need to pay again.
